facts.statement: The genus Haliskia contains only one species, H. peterseni, which is known from a partial skeleton including a skull.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, H. peterseni, known from a partial skeleton with skull.

facts.statement: Haliskia is the most complete pterosaur species known from Australia.
facts.quote: Haliskia represents the most complete pterosaur known from Australia.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Haliskia was discovered by Kevin Petersen in November 2021 near Richmond, Queensland, Australia.
facts.quote: The Haliskia holotype specimen, KK F1426, was discovered by Kevin Petersen in November 2021 within sediments of the Toolebuc Formation (Dig Site 3) near Richmond in Queensland, Australia.

facts.statement: The species name peterseni honors Kevin Petersen, who discovered and prepared the holotype specimen.
facts.quote: The specific name, peterseni, honours Kevin Petersen, the discoverer and preparator of the holotype.

facts.statement: The genus name Haliskia combines Greek words for "sea" and "phantom" or "shadow".
facts.quote: The generic name, Haliskia, combines the Greek words ἅλς (háls), meaning "sea", and σκῐᾱ́ (skiā́), referring to a "phantom", "shadow", or "evil spirit".

facts.statement: Haliskia peterseni was formally described as a new genus and species in 2024 by Pentland et al.
facts.quote: In 2024, Pentland et al. described Haliskia peterseni as a new genus and species of anhanguerian pterosaurs based on these fossil remains.

facts.statement: Based on comparisons with relatives like Arthurdactylus, the estimated wingspan of Haliskia is 4.6 meters.
facts.quote: Based on more complete and proportionally similar relatives such as Arthurdactylus, the wingspan of Haliskia can be estimated at 4.6 m.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses agree that Haliskia is a member of the Ornithocheirae.
facts.quote: Both datasets also agreed that Haliskia can confidently be regarded as a member of the Ornithocheirae.

facts.statement: One phylogenetic analysis places Haliskia and Ferrodraco in a clade sister to the Ornithocheirinae within the Ornithocheiridae.
facts.quote: Using the dataset of Andres (2021), Haliskia and Ferrodraco were found in a clade as the sister to the Ornithocheirinae within the Ornithocheiridae.

facts.statement: Haliskia is classified within the family Anhangueridae.
Haliskia belongs to the subfamily Tropeognathinae.
Haliskia actively inhabited the Eromanga Sea, a large inland sea of Australia.
facts.quote: Habitó activamente el Mar de Eromanga, un gran mar interior de Australia.

facts.statement: Haliskia lived between 106.3 and 100.5 million years ago during the Albian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (106.3 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses of Haliskia have produced significantly different results regarding its evolutionary relationships and clade composition.
facts.quote: Both resulting trees differed significantly in topology, relationships, and clade composition.
